clue.text: What artist's models strike while still working ?

definitions.text: What artist's models strike while still working ?

parts.words: What artist's models strike while still working ?
parts.note: 'strike' suggests industrial action, but models 'strike' attitudes, holding still while the artist is at work

explanation.surface: A question about what life models do on the job when they down tools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' and 'working' together suggest a walkout; in fact models strike attitudes and keep still while the painter works.
explanation.definitionFit: Artist's models hold fixed postures, striking attitudes for the painter.

clue.text: Tip, without being blunt

parts.note: the tip of a pin is its point
less can mean without, as in 'less tax'

explanation.surface: Advice given without being too direct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blunt' looks like it means frank, but here it means lacking a sharp end.
explanation.definitionFit: Something blunt lacks a sharp tip.

clue.text: Mean time?

definitions.meaning: to signify, as in 'this will ... trouble'
a period, as in a ... of fine weather

explanation.definitionFit: To signify trouble is to portend it, and a short period of weather is a stretch of it.

clue.text: The environment is going down…

definitions.meaning: the surroundings or background of something
the sun sinking below the horizon

explanation.surface: The surroundings are deteriorating.
explanation.definitionFit: A story's surroundings are its backdrop; the sun sinks below the horizon at dusk.

clue.text: Parts-of a lady's wardrobe?

definitions.meaning: to part is to divide or split up, a verb in the third person
items of women's clothing such as skirts and blouses sold to be worn in mix-and-match combinations

explanation.surface: Bits and pieces of a woman's clothes collection.
explanation.definitionFit: To divide things is to split them up; mix-and-match skirts and tops are sold as individual garments under that trade name.

clue.text: … in a worse condition — support needed

definitions.meaning: inferior, of lower quality
to back a motion formally in a meeting

explanation.surface: Something in poorer shape that needs propping up.
explanation.definitionFit: Second-rate goods are inferior; backing a motion in a meeting is formally supporting it.

clue.text: Heads going round occupied with artistic affairs

indicators.note: the word for heads encircles the word for occupied

parts.note: pates are heads
a house that is let is rented out, so occupied by tenants

explanation.surface: Heads turning towards people busy with art.
explanation.definitionFit: Painters mix colours on thin boards, the tools of their art.

clue.text: An archdeacon, being in debt, went hungry

indicators.note: the article and title sit inside the colour for debt

parts.note: to be in the red is to be in debt
VEN, Venerable, is an archdeacon's title

explanation.surface: A church official, short of money, could not afford to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: An archdeacon is styled 'the Venerable', abbreviated Ven.
explanation.definitionFit: To raven is to hunt for food greedily, as a famished creature does.

clue.text: Try taking people in at will

parts.note: a test is a try

indicators.note: the word for people goes inside AT

parts.note: men are people

explanation.surface: Trying to bring people round at will.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at will' looks like a phrase, but 'will' alone is the definition: a last will.
explanation.definitionFit: A last will is a formal document disposing of property after death.

clue.text: Quiet about mother's ruin

indicators.note: the word for quiet surrounds the other piece

parts.note: SH is a call for quiet
MA's, mother's

explanation.surface: Keeping quiet about gin, known as mother's ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mother's ruin' is a British nickname for gin; here 'ruin' is the definition and 'mother's' gives MAS.
explanation.definitionFit: To wreck something is to destroy it completely.

clue.text: In dialect it might be the same

indicators.note: the words before could become this word if rearranged, so their letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A remark that a regional way of speaking could make two things alike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it might be' signals that the letters of IN DIALECT can be rearranged into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that match exactly are alike in every respect, without any difference.

clue.text: View point, in the Life of Caesar

indicators.note: the compass point is placed within the Latin word for life

parts.note: Caesar spoke Latin, in which life is VITA
S, south, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A vantage point mentioned in a biography of Julius Caesar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'View point' reads as one term, but 'View' is the definition and 'point' is a compass point, S.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospect or panorama is a broad scene seen from a vantage.

clue.text: How are the mighty fallen! David's D. notice

definitions.text: How are the mighty fallen! David's D. notice

parts.words: How are the mighty fallen! David's D. notice
parts.note: King David's lament for Saul and Jonathan asks that news of their deaths be kept from the Philistine city, like a government request to suppress a story

explanation.surface: A news-gagging order issued by King David over the fall of the great.
explanation.walkthrough: A D-notice is a British government request to editors not to publish something sensitive; in 2 Samuel 1:20 David asks that Saul's death not be proclaimed in the Philistine city.
explanation.definitionFit: The quotation comes from David's lament in Samuel, which also says how the mighty are fallen, asking the Philistines not to hear.

clue.text: Combine after note issue

indicators.note: the word for combine is placed following the musical note

parts.note: E is one of the notes of the musical scale
to combine is to merge

explanation.surface: An instruction to join things up once a memo has gone out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' looks like a noun ending the surface but is the verb: to come out.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue forth is to come out or appear from somewhere.

clue.text: Angle for dignity

definitions.meaning: the angle of a gun barrel or a line of sight above the horizontal
raised rank or exalted status

explanation.surface: Looking for an angle to gain dignity.
explanation.definitionFit: The upward angle of a gun is its altitude setting; a raising in rank gives exalted status.

clue.text: Uncalled for, and tries the patience of a saint

parts.note: to needle someone is to annoy them

explanation.surface: Something unnecessary that would exasperate even the most patient person.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uncalled for is unnecessary, not required at all.

clue.text: The French, up against fringes with cloth borders

indicators.note: in a down clue the French article is read from bottom to top

parts.note: LES is French for 'the' (plural)
V, versus, means against
edges are fringes

explanation.surface: French people rising up against fringe groups over cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: The finished woven margins of fabric stop it fraying.

clue.text: A scheme to fascinate us ?

definitions.meaning: a secret plot
to arouse our curiosity

explanation.surface: A plot designed to captivate us.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret plot is a conspiracy; arousing curiosity is fascinating someone.

clue.text: Try to celebrate all round -by stripping ?

indicators.note: the word for celebrate goes around the word for try

parts.note: to sing of something is to celebrate it
a judge will hear, or try, a case

explanation.surface: Someone attempting to party while taking their clothes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' is the legal sense: a court hears a case. 'stripping' is the removal of a sheep's fleece.
explanation.definitionFit: Clipping the wool from a sheep strips it of its fleece.

clue.text: Disconcerts with these car noises

definitions.meaning: unsettles or flusters someone
the clattering sounds of loose parts in a vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone is unsettled by the sounds their car makes.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsettling someone flusters them, and loose parts clatter in a moving vehicle.

clue.text: Like the Old Man in a tree's bee

definitions.text: Like the Old Man in a tree's bee

parts.words: Like the Old Man in a tree's bee
parts.note: in Edward Lear's limerick an old man in a tree is pestered by a bee he calls a regular brute

explanation.surface: Describing the insect that bothered an old man perched in a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Lear's limerick 'There was an Old Man in a tree, Who was horribly bored by a Bee' ends with the bee being called 'a regular brute of a Bee'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lear's bee is called a brute, so it is savage and cruel in character.

clue.text: Surveys of opinion 'in a legal affair

parts.note: RE, as in 'in re', means in the matter of in legal usage
views are opinions

explanation.surface: Polls taken on what people think about a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: Critical assessments look over and appraise something.

clue.text: Generally, wanting the lot is involved with power

indicators.note: lacking the letters for the whole lot, so those are removed
the remaining letters are tangled into a new order

parts.note: all is the lot

explanation.surface: Broadly, not wanting everything is tied up with authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' takes ALL out of GENERALLY, leaving GENERY, and 'is involved' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Physics measures capacity for work as force or strength.

clue.text: Elements of literature-exact reference

definitions.meaning: books are divided into sections and poems into lines
a precise citation, as of a Bible text by section and line number

explanation.surface: The building blocks of writing, and a precise citation.
explanation.definitionFit: Books divide into numbered sections and lines, and quoting both numbers gives a precise source for a text.

clue.text: Contend with the right

definitions.meaning: to assert or maintain
an entitlement to something

explanation.surface: Arguing with someone who is correct.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert something is to maintain it; an entitlement is a demand one may lawfully make.

clue.text: A German flower in a Somerset ditch

definitions.meaning: a flower here is something that flows, a river in Germany
in Somerset, a county in south-west England, a drainage channel on the Levels is called by this name

explanation.surface: A German bloom growing in a ditch in Somerset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is crossword shorthand for a river, something that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: The great river flows through Germany; Somerset's drainage channels share its name.

clue.text: He lay in a cowslip's bell — sounds heavenly!

definitions.text: He lay in a cowslip's bell

indicators.note: the clue says the word for heavenly is spoken, giving a name that is pronounced like it

parts.note: aerial, of the air or sky, can mean heavenly

explanation.surface: A tiny figure sleeping in a flower, who sounds celestial.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's The Tempest the airy spirit sings 'In a cowslip's bell I lie'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's sprite in The Tempest sings that he lies in a cowslip's bell.

clue.text: The oldest profession-a hobby with Flora

definitions.meaning: Adam tilled the Garden of Eden, so tending plants is the first job
Flora is the Roman goddess of flowers, so the pastime involves plants

explanation.surface: A coy reference to prostitution, then a pastime shared with a woman named Flora.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The oldest profession' is a euphemism for prostitution; here it means Adam's work in Eden.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam was set to tend Eden, the first job; tending plants and flowers is also a popular pastime.

clue.text: Some men join in order to live there

definitions.text: Some men join in order to live there

parts.words: Some men join in order to live there
parts.note: 'in order to' reads as purpose, but the men join a religious order and live in its house

explanation.surface: Some men sign up for something just to get somewhere to live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order to' looks like the phrase meaning 'so as to'; the men join a religious order.
explanation.definitionFit: Monks who join a religious order live in its community house.

clue.text: Filters-consult the footnote

parts.note: to see a doctor is to consult one
PS, postscript, is a note added at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: An instruction to read the note at the bottom about filters.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid that filters through soaks slowly out or trickles.
